paragraphs: Waste Management, Inc. is a holding company and all operations are conducted by its subsidiaries. When the terms "the Company," "we," "us" or "our" are used in this document, those terms refer to Waste Management, Inc., together with its consolidated subsidiaries and consolidated variable interest entities. When we use the term "WMI," we are referring only to Waste Management, Inc., the parent holding company.

WMI was incorporated in Oklahoma in 1987 under the name "USA Waste Services, Inc." and was reincorporated as a Delaware company in 1995. In a 1998 merger, the Illinois-based waste services company formerly known as Waste Management, Inc. became a wholly-owned subsidiary of WMI and changed its name to Waste Management Holdings, Inc. ("WM Holdings"). At the same time, our parent holding company changed its name from USA Waste Services to Waste Management, Inc. Like WMI, WM Holdings is a holding company and all operations are conducted by subsidiaries.

Our principal executive offices are located at 800 Capitol Street, Suite 3000, Houston, Texas 77002. Our telephone number is (713) 512-6200. Our website address is www.wm.com. Our annual reports on Form 10-K, quarterly reports on Form 10-Q and current reports on Form 8-K are all available, free of charge, on our website as soon as practicable after we file the reports with the SEC. Our stock is traded on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol "WM."

We are North America's leading provider of comprehensive environmental solutions, providing services throughout the United States ("U.S.") and Canada. We partner with our customers and the communities we serve to manage and reduce waste at each stage from collection to disposal, while recovering valuable resources and creating clean, renewable energy. Our solid waste business is operated and managed locally by our subsidiaries that focus on distinct geographic areas and provide collection, transfer, disposal, recycling and resource recovery services. Through our Waste Management Renewable Energy ("Renewable Energy") segment, we are also a leading developer, operator and owner of landfill gas-to-energy facilities in the U.S. and Canada that produce renewable electricity and renewable natural gas ("RNG"), which is a significant source of fuel that we allocate to our natural gas fleet. Following our 2024 acquisition of Stericycle, Inc. ("Stericycle"), our Healthcare Solutions segment provides regulated waste and compliance services ("RWCS") and secure information destruction ("SID") services in the U.S., Canada and Western Europe that protect people and brands, promote health and well-being and safeguard the environment. Additionally, through our Recycling Processing and Sales segment, we are a leading recycler in the U.S. and Canada, handling materials that include paper, cardboard, glass, plastic and metal. During 2025, our largest customer represented less than 5% of annual revenues.

We own or operate 257 landfill sites, which is the largest network of landfills throughout the U.S. and Canada. In order to make disposal more practical for larger urban markets, where the distance to landfills is typically farther, we manage 342 transfer stations, excluding those acquired from Stericycle, that consolidate, compact and transport waste efficiently and economically. We also use waste to create energy, recovering the gas produced naturally as waste decomposes in landfills and using the gas in generators to make electricity. We are a leading recycler in the U.S. and Canada, handling materials that include cardboard, paper, glass, plastic and metal. We provide cost-efficient, environmentally sound recycling programs for municipalities, businesses and households across the U.S. and Canada as well as other services that supplement our solid waste business.

Our fundamental strategy has not changed; we remain dedicated to providing long-term value to our stockholders by successfully executing our core strategy of focused differentiation and continuous improvement. We have enabled a people-first, technology-led focus to drive our mission to maximize resource value, while minimizing environmental impact, and sustainability and environmental stewardship is embedded in all that we do. Our strategy leverages and sustains the strongest asset network in the industry to drive best-in-class customer experience and growth. Our strategic planning processes appropriately consider that the future of our business and the industry can be influenced by changes in economic conditions, the competitive landscape, the regulatory environment, asset and resource availability and technology. We believe that focused differentiation, which is driven by capitalizing on our unique and extensive network of assets, will deliver profitable growth and position us to leverage competitive advantages. Simultaneously, we believe that investing in

automation to improve processes and drive operational efficiency combined with a focus on the cost to serve our customers will yield an attractive profit margin and enhanced service quality. We are furthering our strategy of focused differentiation and continuous improvement beyond our traditional waste operations through our sustainability growth strategy that includes significant investments in our Renewable Energy and Recycling Processing and Sales segments, while increasing automation and reducing labor dependency. In addition, with our acquisition of Stericycle, we have advanced our growth strategy and built upon our sustainability initiatives. The acquisition provides a complementary business platform in medical waste, a sector with attractive near- and long-term growth dynamics, and in secure information destruction services to further our leading suite of comprehensive waste and environmental solutions. Furthermore, we continue to evaluate and plan to pursue emerging diversion technologies that may generate additional value.

Our Company's goals are targeted at putting our people first, positioning them to serve and care for our customers, the environment, the communities in which we work and our stockholders. Our brand promise is ALWAYS WORKING FOR A SUSTAINABLE TOMORROW®. We live this promise through our service offerings and sustainable solutions, our investments in innovation, our people and our commitment to the future. Through our longtime focus on finding sustainable solutions, we continue to evolve beyond being a traditional environmental waste services company. Increasingly, our industry-leading focus on environmental sustainability aligns with demand from our customers who want more of their waste materials recovered. Waste streams are becoming more complex, and our aim is to address current needs, while anticipating the expanding and evolving needs of our customers. We believe we are uniquely equipped to meet the challenges of the changing waste industry and our customers' waste management needs, both today and tomorrow as we work together to envision and create a more sustainable future.

We believe that execution of our strategy will deliver shareholder value and leadership in a dynamic industry and in any economic environment. In addition, we intend to continue to return value to our stockholders through dividend payments and share repurchases. In December 2025, we announced that our Board of Directors expects to increase the quarterly dividend from $0.825 to $0.945 per share for dividends declared in 2026, which is a 14.5% increase from the quarterly dividends we declared in 2025. This is an indication of our ability to generate strong and consistent cash flows and marks the 23rd consecutive year of dividend increases. All quarterly dividends will be declared at the discretion of our Board of Directors and depend on various factors, including our net earnings, financial condition, cash required for future business plans, growth and acquisitions and other factors the Board of Directors may deem relevant. Additionally, given the substantial progress already made on leverage reduction following the Stericycle acquisition, we resumed share repurchases in February 2026. Our Board of Directors approved up to $3.0 billion in future share repurchases, exclusive of fees, commissions and taxes. This new authorization supersedes and replaces the remaining authority under the prior Board of Directors' authorization for share repurchases announced in December 2023. Under this new authorization, we currently expect to repurchase approximately $2.0 billion of shares during 2026, while continuing to prioritize a return to our targeted leverage level during the year. The amount of future share repurchases executed under our Board of Directors' authorization is determined in management's discretion, based on various factors, including our leverage level, net earnings, financial condition and cash required for future business plans, growth and acquisitions.

Our future financial performance and success are dependent in large part upon our ability to implement our business strategy successfully. Implementation of our strategy will require effective management of our operational, financial and human resources and will place significant demands on those resources. See Item 1. Business for more information on our business strategy. There are risks involved in pursuing our strategy, including the following:
● Our employees, customers or investors may not embrace and support our strategy.

● A key element of our strategy is yield management through focus on price leadership, which has presented challenges to keep existing business and win new business at reasonable returns. Our unwillingness to pursue lower margin volumes may negatively affect our cash flows or results of operations.
● We may be unsuccessful in implementing our technology-led automation and optimization strategy and other improvements to operational efficiency and such efforts may not yield the intended result.
● We may not be able to maintain cost savings achieved, including through our automation and optimization or acquisition integration efforts, due to inflationary cost pressures or otherwise.

On November 4, 2024, we completed our acquisition of all outstanding shares of Stericycle for $62.00 per share in cash, pursuant to an Agreement and Plan of Merger dated June 3, 2024. Total enterprise value of the acquisition was $7.2 billion (net of cash acquired) when including the assumption of $0.5 billion of debt and the repayment of approximately $0.8 billion of net debt. The acquisition expanded our offerings in the U.S., Canada and parts of Western Europe. The post-closing operating results of Stericycle have been included in our Consolidated Financial Statements within our Healthcare Solutions segment.

For the year ended December 31, 2025, we incurred acquisition and integration related costs of $120 million, comprised of $89 million of selling, general and administrative costs and $31 million of restructuring costs. For the year ended December 31, 2024, we incurred acquisition and integration related costs of $160 million, which were primarily classified as selling, general and administrative expenses.Refer to Note 19 for more information on the performance of our Healthcare Solutions segment.

Our Collection and Disposal businesses provide integrated environmental services, including collection, transfer and disposal. We evaluate our Collection and Disposal businesses primarily through two geographic segments, East Tier and West Tier. Our East Tier primarily consists of geographic areas located in the Eastern U.S., the Great Lakes region and substantially all of Canada. Our West Tier primarily includes geographic areas located in the Western, Southern and Central U.S., including the upper Midwest region, and British Columbia, Canada. Additionally, we provide Other Ancillary services that are not managed through the Tier segments but that support our collection and disposal operations. Other Ancillary includes specialized services performed for customers that have differentiated needs. These specialized services are targeted at large industrial customers managed through our Sustainability and Environmental Solutions ("SES") business or geographically dispersed customers managed through our Strategic Business Solutions ("WMSBS") business. Also included within Other Ancillary are the results of non-operating entities that provide financial assurance and self-insurance support for our business, net of intercompany activity.

Our Collection and Disposal businesses' operating revenues are primarily generated from fees charged for our collection, transfer and disposal. Revenues from our collection operations are influenced by factors such as collection frequency, type of collection equipment furnished, type and volume or weight of the waste collected, distance to the disposal facility or recycling facility and our disposal costs. Revenues from our landfill operations consist of tipping fees, which are generally based on the type and weight or volume of waste deposited, considering our cost of loading, transporting and disposing of the solid waste at a disposal site. Fees charged at transfer stations are generally based on the weight or volume of waste deposited, considering our cost of loading, transporting and disposing of the solid waste at a disposal site. The fees we charge for our services generally include applicable fees, such as our energy surcharge, which are intended to pass through to customers for direct and indirect costs incurred.

Included within our Collection and Disposal businesses are landfills having (i) 19 third-party power generating facilities converting our landfill gas to fuel electricity generators; (ii) 17 third-party RNG facilities processing landfill gas to be sold to natural gas suppliers and (iii) nine third-party projects delivering our landfill gas by pipeline to industrial customers as a direct substitute for fossil fuels in industrial processes. In return for providing our landfill gas, we receive royalties from each facility, including the benefit of a 15% royalty from our Renewable Energy segment based on net operating revenue generated through the sale of RNG, renewable identification numbers ("RINs"), electricity and capacity, Renewable Energy Credits ("RECs") and related environmental attributes from the 86 landfill beneficial use renewable energy projects owned by Renewable Energy on our active landfills, which is eliminated in consolidation.

Our Recycling Processing and Sales segment includes the processing and sales of materials collected from residential, commercial and industrial customers. The materials are delivered to and processed at one of our many recycling facilities. Through our brokerage business, we also manage the marketing of recycling commodities that are processed in our facilities and by third parties by maintaining comprehensive service centers that continuously analyze market prices, logistics, market demands and product quality.

Recycling Processing and Sales revenues generally consist of tipping fees and the sale of recycling commodities to and/or on behalf of third parties. Our Recycling Processing and Sales segment excludes the collection of recycled materials from our residential, commercial, and industrial customers which is included within our Collection and Disposal businesses.

Our Renewable Energy segment develops, operates and promotes projects for the beneficial use of landfill gas. Landfill gas is produced naturally as waste decomposes in a landfill. The methane component of the landfill gas is a readily available, renewable energy source that can be gathered and used beneficially as an alternative to fossil fuel. Renewable Energy converts landfill gas into several sources of renewable energy which include RNG, electricity and capacity, heat and/or steam. Renewable Energy also generates (i) RINs under the Renewable Fuel Standard ("RFS") program; (ii) other credits under a variety of state programs associated with the use of RNG in our compressed natural gas fleet and (iii) RECs associated with the production of electricity. The RINs, RECs, and other credits are sold to counterparties who are obligated under the regulatory programs and have a responsibility to procure RINs, RECs, and other credits proportionate to their fossil fuel production and imports. RINs and RECs prices generally fluctuate in response to regulations enacted by the Environmental Protection Agency ("EPA") or other regulatory bodies, as well as changes in supply and demand.

As of December 31, 2025, we had 103 landfill gas beneficial use projects producing commercial quantities of methane gas at owned or operated landfills. For 62 of these projects, the processed gas is used to fuel electricity generators. The electricity is then sold to public utilities, municipal utilities or power cooperatives. For 24 of these projects, the gas is used at the landfill or delivered by pipeline to industrial customers as a direct substitute for fossil fuels in industrial processes. For 17 of these projects, the landfill gas is processed to pipeline quality RNG and then sold to natural gas suppliers. Additionally, three projects are on third-party landfills. The revenues from these facilities are primarily generated through (i) the sale of captured and converted landfill methane gas; (ii) the sale of RINs under the RFS program implemented by the EPA; (iii) sale of Low Carbon Fuel credits designed to stimulate the use of low-carbon fuels and (iv) the sale of energy (electricity and capacity) and associated RECs. Renewable Energy is charged a 15% royalty on net operating revenue from these facilities residing on our active and closed landfills from our Collection and Disposal and Corporate and Other businesses, which is eliminated in consolidation. Additionally, Renewable Energy operates and maintains six third-party landfill beneficial gas use projects in return for service revenue. Our Collection and Disposal and Corporate and Other businesses benefit from these projects as well as 54 additional third-party landfill beneficial gas use projects in the form of royalties.

Our Healthcare Solutions segment includes (i) RWCS which provide compliance programs and collection, processing, and disposal of regulated and specialized waste, including medical, pharmaceutical and hazardous waste and (ii) SID services, which provide for the collection of personal and confidential information for secure destruction and recycling of sorted office paper. While the Healthcare Solutions businesses manage large volumes of waste and other materials, the average volume per customer site is relatively small.
Waste Management, Inc. 為一間控股公司，所有營運均透過其子公司進行。當本文件中使用 "the Company," "we," "us" 或 "our" 這些詞語時，這些詞語指的是 Waste Management, Inc.，包括其合併子公司及合併可變利益實體。當我們使用 "WMI" 這個詞語時，我們僅指 Waste Management, Inc.，即母公司。

WMI 於 1987 年在奧克拉荷馬州註冊成立，當時的公司名稱為 "USA Waste Services, Inc."，並於 1995 年重新註冊為德拉瓦州公司。在 1998 年的合併中，原本位於伊利諾州的廢棄物服務公司，當時名為 Waste Management, Inc.，成為 WMI 的 wholly-owned 子公司，並更名為 Waste Management Holdings, Inc. ("WM Holdings"). 同時，我們的母公司更名為 Waste Management, Inc.。與 WMI 一樣，WM Holdings 也為一間控股公司，所有營運均透過子公司進行。

我們的總部位於德克薩斯州休士頓市 800 Capitol Street, Suite 3000。電話號碼為 (713) 512-6200。我們的網站地址為 www.wm.com。我們的年度報告（Form 10-K）、季報（Form 10-Q）及現況報告（Form 8-K）均於向美國證券交易委員會（SEC）提交後，盡速在網站上提供，免費供下載。我們的股票在紐約證券交易所（New York Stock Exchange）交易，代碼為 "WM."

我們是北美地區提供全面環境解決方案的領導者，服務範圍遍及美國（"U.S.") 和加拿大。我們與客戶及所服務的社區合作，從收集到處置的每個階段管理並減少廢棄物，同時回收有價值的資源並創造清潔、可再生能源。我們的固體廢棄物業務由專注於特定地理區域的子公司進行營運與管理，提供收集、轉運、處置、回收及資源回收服務。透過我們的 Waste Management Renewable Energy ("Renewable Energy") 分部，我們也是美國和加拿大 landfill gas-to-energy 儲存設施的主要開發者、營運者及所有者，這些設施產生可再生能源電力及可再生能源天然氣（"RNG"），這是我們分配給天然氣車隊的重要燃料來源。在 2024 年收購 Stericycle, Inc. ("Stericycle") 後，我們的醫療解決方案分部提供受規範廢棄物及合規服務（"RWCS"）及安全資訊銷毀（"SID"）服務，服務範圍包括美國、加拿大及西歐，保護人們與品牌，促進健康與福祉，並 safeguard 環境。此外，透過我們的回收處理與銷售分部，我們是美國和加拿大主要的回收商，處理的材料包括紙張、紙箱、玻璃、塑膠及金屬。在 2025 年，我們最大的客戶佔年度營收的比例低於 5%。

我們擁有或營運 257 個垃圾掩埋場，這是美國和加拿大最大的垃圾掩埋場網路。為使較大都會區的處置更為實用，因這些地區到垃圾掩埋場的距離通常較遠，我們管理 342 個轉運站（不計從 Stericycle 收購的轉運站），這些轉運站可將廢棄物集中、壓縮並高效且經濟地運輸。我們也利用廢棄物產生能源，回收垃圾掩埋場中廢棄物自然分解產生的氣體，並將該氣體用於發電機產生電力。我們是美國和加拿大主要的回收商，處理的材料包括紙箱、紙張、玻璃、塑膠及金屬。我們為美國和加拿大各級政府、企業及家庭提供成本效益高且環境友善的回收方案，以及補充我們固體廢棄物業務的其他服務。

我們的基本戰略並未改變；我們仍致力於透過成功執行我們的核心戰略，即專注差異化與持續改善，為股東創造長期價值。我們已實現以人為本、科技為導向的重點，以推動我們的使命，即最大化資源價值，同時減少環境影響。可持續性與環境責任已內建於我們所有行動中。我們的戰略依賴並維持行業中最強大的資產網路，以推動最佳客戶體驗與成長。我們的戰略規劃過程適當考慮到未來業務與產業的發展可能受到經濟條件變化、競爭環境、法規環境、資產與資源可得性及科技的影響。我們相信，透過善用我們獨特且廣泛的資產網路，專注差異化將帶來可盈利的成長，並使我們能利用競爭優勢。同時，我們相信投資於

自動化以改善流程並推動運營效率，結合對服務客戶成本的關注，將產生有吸引力的毛利率與提升的服務品質。我們進一步透過我們的可持續性成長戰略，將專注差異化與持續改善的戰略延伸至我們傳統的廢棄物業務之外，這包括對我們的 Renewable Energy 與 Recycling Processing and Sales 分部的重大投資，同時增加自動化並減少勞動力依賴。此外，透過我們收購 Stericycle，我們已推進我們的成長戰略並加強我們的可持續性計畫。此次收購提供了一個在醫療廢棄物領域的補充性業務平台，該領域具有吸引人的短期與長期成長動力，並在安全資訊銷毀服務方面進一步強化我們的領先全面廢棄物與環境解決方案組合。此外，我們持續評估並計畫追求可能產生額外價值的創新廢棄物分流技術。

我們公司的目標是將我們的員工放在首位，使他們能服務並關懷我們的客戶、環境、我們工作的社區及股東。我們的品牌承諾是 ALWAYS WORKING FOR A SUSTAINABLE TOMORROW®。我們透過我們的服務方案與可持續解決方案、我們對創新投資、我們的員工及我們對未來的承諾來實踐這項承諾。透過我們長期以來對尋找可持續解決方案的關注，我們持續進化，超越傳統的環境廢棄物服務公司。越來越多地，我們在環境可持續性方面的行業領先地位與我們客戶的需求相呼應，這些客戶希望回收更多廢棄物材料。廢棄物流變得越來越複雜，我們的目標是解決當前需求，同時預見我們客戶不斷擴展與進化的需求。我們相信我們獨特地具備應對變化的廢棄物產業及客戶廢棄物管理需求的挑戰，無論是今天還是未來，當我們一起展望並創造一個更可持續的未來。

我們相信執行我們的策略將為股東創造價值並在動態產業與任何經濟環境中取得領導地位。此外，我們意圖持續透過股息支付與股票回購回報股東價值。2025年12月，我們宣佈本公司董事會預期將提高2026年宣告的每季股息從每股0.825美元至0.945美元，這相當於2025年每季宣告股息的14.5%增幅。這顯示我們產生強而穩定現金流的能力，並標誌著連續23年股息增加的紀錄。所有每季股息將由本公司董事會視情況宣告，並取決於多種因素，包括本公司淨收入、財務狀況、未來業務計畫所需的現金、成長與收購及其他董事會認為相關的因素。此外，考慮到在Stericycle收購後已取得顯著的減債進展，我們於2026年2月恢復股票回購。本公司董事會批准未來最高30億美元的股票回購授權，不包括費用、佣金及稅務。此新授權取代並取代2023年12月宣佈的先前董事會授權的剩餘股票回購權限。根據此新授權，我們目前預期於2026年回購約20億美元的股票，同時持續優先回復我們目標的負債水平。未來根據董事會授權執行的股票回購金額，由管理層視情況決定，並根據多種因素，包括本公司負債水平、淨收入、財務狀況及未來業務計畫所需的現金、成長與收購。

我們高階管理層透過五個應報告分部評估、監督與管理我們業務的財務表現，這些分部被稱為(i) 收集與處置 - 東階層("East Tier"); (ii) 收集與處置 - 西階層("West Tier"); (iii) 回收處理與銷售; (iv) 可再生能源與(v) 健康照護解決方案。我們的東階層與西階層，加上某些非由階層分部管理但支援我們收集與處置作業的輔助服務("Other Ancillary")，組成我們的"收集與處置"業務。
我們的東階層主要由位於美國東部、五大湖地區以及加拿大絕大部分地區的地理區域組成。我們的西階層主要包括位於美國西部、南部與中部地區，包括上密西根地區，以及加拿大不列顛哥倫比亞省的地理區域。
我們也提供一些未經我們五個應報告分部管理的附加服務，這些服務被列為企業及其他。如需進一步討論，請參閱我們合併財務報表的附註19。
透過我們的收集與處置業務提供的服務如下所述：
收集。我們對客戶的承諾從廣泛的廢棄物收集網路開始。收集涉及從產生地點將廢棄物與可回收物、建築與拆除廢料以及有機材料運送到轉運站、回收設施或處置場。我們通常在兩種類型的安排下提供收集服務：

paragraphs: 本節包含我們於2025年12月31日財務年度之營運成果討論。此討論可能包含前瞻性陳述。請參閱本年度報告10-K表單第一部分之「關於前瞻性陳述之警示聲明」以取得更多資訊。前瞻性陳述可能受到某些風險與不確定性影響，這些風險與不確定性可能導致實際結果與我們過去經驗或目前預期或預期結果有重大差異。這些風險與不確定性包括，但不僅限於，第一部分第1A項「風險因素」及其他處於本報告中所描述的風險與不確定性，也可能在未來報告中不時於美國證券交易委員會（SEC）提交之報告中描述。請考量這些披露內容，並與合併財務報表及其附註一併閱讀。
關於我們於2024年12月31日財務年度與2023年12月31日財務年度之營運成果比較，請參閱我們2024年財務年度年度報告10-K表單第二部分第7項「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析」。

我們是北美地區提供全面環境解決方案的領導者，主要於美國（U.S.）與加拿大提供相關服務。我們與客戶及所服務之社區合作，於從收集到處置之各階段管理並減少廢棄物，同時回收寶貴資源並創造清潔、可再生能源。我們擁有或營運美國與加拿大最大規模之垃圾掩埋場網路。為使較大都會區市場之處置更為實際，因這些地區至掩埋場之距離通常較遠，我們管理轉運站以有效且經濟地集中、壓縮並運輸廢棄物。我們之固體廢棄物業務由專注於特定地理區域之子公司進行營運與管理，提供收集、轉運、處置、回收與資源回收服務。透過我們之廢棄物管理再生能源（Renewable Energy）業務部門，我們也是美國與加拿大 landfill gas-to-energy 廠場的領導開發、營運與所有者，這些廠場產生可再生能源電力與可再生能源天然氣（RNG），這是我們分配至天然氣車隊之重要燃料來源。於2024年我們收購Stericycle, Inc.（Stericycle）後，我們之醫療解決方案部門提供受規範廢棄物與合規服務（RWCS）及安全資訊銷毀（SID）服務，服務範圍包括美國、加拿大與西歐，以保護人與品牌、促進健康與福祉並 safeguards 環境。此外，透過我們之回收處理與銷售部門，我們是美國與加拿大之領導回收商，處理材料包括紙張、紙箱、玻璃、塑膠與金屬。

我們之高階管理層透過五個應報告分部評估、監督與管理我們業務之財務表現，這些分部稱為（i）收集與處置－東區（East Tier）；（ii）收集與處置－西區（West Tier）；（iii）回收處理與銷售；（iv）再生能源；（v）醫療解決方案。我們之東區與西區，加上某些輔助服務（Other Ancillary）並非透過我們之Tier分部管理，但支援我們之收集與處置作業，組成我們之「收集與處置」業務。我們亦提供其他非透過五個應報告分部管理之服務，這些服務以「公司與其他」（Corporate and Other）呈現。

我們於2024年11月4日完成收購Stericycle, Inc.（Stericycle）所有發行在外之股權，每股現金價格為62.00美元，根據2024年6月3日簽訂之合併協議與計劃。此收購之總企業價值為72億美元（扣除所收購之現金）包含假設收購0.5億美元債務與償還約0.8億美元淨債務。此收購擴展我們於美國、加拿大與西歐部分地區之服務項目。收購後之Stericycle營運結果已納入我們之合併財務報表中之醫療解決方案分部。
於2025年12月31日財務年度，我們產生與收購及整合相關之費用1.2億美元，包含8900萬美元之銷售、一般及行政費用與3100萬美元之重整費用。於2024年12月31日財務年度，我們產生與收購及整合相關之費用1.6億美元，主要歸類為銷售、一般及行政費用。請參閱附註19以取得更多關於我們醫療解決方案分部表現之資訊。

我們之收集與處置業務提供整合式環境服務，包括收集、轉運與處置。我們主要透過兩個地理分部評估我們之收集與處置業務，即東區與西區。我們之東區主要包含位於美國東部、五大湖地區與加拿大絕大部分地區。我們之西區主要包含位於美國西部、南部與中部地區，包括上中西部地區，以及加拿大不列顛哥倫比亞省。此外，我們提供Other Ancillary服務，這些服務並非透過Tier分部管理，但支援我們之收集與處置作業。Other Ancillary包含為有特殊需求之客戶所提供的專業服務。這些專業服務針對大型工業客戶，由我們之永續與環境解決方案（SES）業務管理，或針對地理分散之客戶，由我們之戰略業務解決方案（WMSBS）業務管理。Other Ancillary亦包含提供財務保證與自負風險支援之非營運實體之結果，扣除內部交易活動。

我們之收集與處置業務之營運收入主要來自於我們之收集、轉運與處置服務所收取之費用。我們之收集作業收入受多種因素影響，例如收集頻率、所提供的收集設備類型、收集之廢棄物類型與重量或體積、至處置場或回收場之距離以及我們之處置成本。我們之掩埋場作業收入包含傾倒費用，通常根據所存放廢棄物之類型與重量或體積計算，考量我們之裝載、運輸與處置固體廢棄物於處置場之成本。轉運站所收取之費用通常根據所存放廢棄物之重量或體積計算，考量我們之裝載、運輸與處置固體廢棄物於處置場之成本。我們所收取之服務費用通常包含適用之費用，例如我們之能源附加費，這些費用旨在將直接與間接成本轉嫁給客戶。

包含於我們的收運與處置業務中的是垃圾掩埋場，其包含 (i) 19 個第三方電力發電設施，將我們的垃圾掩埋氣轉換為發電機燃料；(ii) 17 個第三方 RNG 設施，處理垃圾掩埋氣以供出售給天然氣供應商，以及 (iii) 九個第三方專案，透過管線將我們的垃圾掩埋氣直接作為工業流程中化石燃料的替代品供應給工業客戶。為提供垃圾掩埋氣，我們從每個設施獲得特許權使用費，包括來自我們可再生能源業務的 15% 特許權使用費，基於透過出售 RNG、可再生能源識別數字 ("RINs" )、電力與容量、可再生能源憑證 ("RECs" ) 以及相關環境屬性所產生的淨營運收入，來自 Renewable Energy 所擁有且位於我們現有垃圾掩埋場的 86 個垃圾掩埋氣有益使用可再生能源專案，此部分在合併時已抵銷。
我們的回收處理與銷售業務包括從住宅、商業及工業客戶收集的材料之處理與銷售。這些材料會運送到我們的許多回收設施之一進行處理。透過我們的經紀業務，我們也管理這些在我們設施內或由第三方處理的回收材料之市場行銷，透過維護全面的服務中心持續分析市場價格、物流、市場需求與產品品質。
回收處理與銷售收入通常包含傾倒費用以及向第三方或代表第三方出售回收材料。我們的回收處理與銷售業務不包含從住宅、商業及工業客戶收集回收材料，此部分包含於我們的收運與處置業務中。

我們的可再生能源業務開發、營運與推廣垃圾掩埋氣的有益使用專案。垃圾掩埋氣是在垃圾掩埋場中廢棄物分解時自然產生的。垃圾掩埋氣中的甲烷成分是一種 readily available、可再生能源來源，可以收集並用作替代化石燃料的有益能源。可再生能源將垃圾掩埋氣轉換為多種可再生能源，包括 RNG、電力與容量、熱能與/或蒸汽。可再生能源也產生 (i) 在可再生能源燃料標準 ("RFS" ) 程式下的 RINs；(ii) 在多種州政府程式下與我們壓縮天然氣車隊使用 RNG 相關的其他憑證，以及 (iii) 與電力生產相關的 RECs。RINs、RECs 與其他憑證會出售給負有義務參與監管程式並需按比例取得 RINs、RECs 與其他憑證的對手方。RINs 與 RECs 的價格通常會因環境保護局 ("EPA" ) 或其他監管機構所頒布的法規，以及供應與需求的變化而波動。

截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們共有 103 個垃圾掩埋氣有益使用專案，於我們擁有或營運的垃圾掩埋場中產生商業規模的甲烷氣。其中 62 個專案的處理氣體用於發電機燃料。電力隨後出售給公共電力公司、市立電力公司或電力合作社。其中 24 個專案的氣體用於垃圾掩埋場內或透過管線供應給工業客戶，作為工業流程中化石燃料的直接替代品。其中 17 個專案的垃圾掩埋氣被處理成管線品質的 RNG，然後出售給天然氣供應商。此外，有三個專案位於第三方垃圾掩埋場。這些設施的收入主要來自 (i) 捕獲並轉換的垃圾掩埋甲烷氣出售；(ii) 根據 EPA 頒布的 RFS 程式出售 RINs；(iii) 出售低碳燃料憑證以促進低碳燃料的使用，以及 (iv) 電力 (電力與容量) 及相關 RECs 的出售。可再生能源業務從我們現有及已關閉垃圾掩埋場的這些設施中，根據我們收運與處置及企業與其他業務的淨營運收入收取 15% 的特許權使用費，此部分在合併時已抵銷。此外，可再生能源業務經營並維護六個第三方垃圾掩埋氣有益使用專案，以換取服務收入。我們的收運與處置及企業與其他業務也受益於這些專案以及 54 個額外的第三方垃圾掩埋氣有益使用專案，形式為特許權使用費。
我們的醫療解決方案業務包括 (i) RWCS，提供合規計畫與醫療、藥品及危險廢棄物等受管制與專業廢棄物的收集、處理與處置，以及 (ii) SID 服務，提供個人與機密資訊的收集，以進行安全銷毀與回收分類辦公室紙張。雖然醫療解決方案業務管理大量廢棄物與其他材料，但每個客戶場地的平均體積相對較小。

headings: 若我們未能落實本公司商業策略，將可能對財務表現與成長造成重大且不利的影響。
我們可能無法實現從Stericycle收購所預期的戰略效益、營收與獲利成長，或成本協同效益。
本公司業務面臨營運與安全風險，包括員工及其他人員受傷的風險。
本公司業務具有季節性，氣候變遷所導致的極端天氣事件及活動驅動型專案，將導致營收結果波動，過去表現未必能反映未來結果。
對永續性表現與揭露的關注與規範，可能導致成本增加、違規風險、聲譽受損及相關不利影響。
環境服務產業競爭激烈，若我們無法在市場中成功競爭，將可能對本公司業務、財務狀況與營運結果造成重大且不利的影響。
本公司營業收入、獲利及現金流會因商品價格變動及需求變化而波動，未來可能無預警地大幅波動。
客戶對替代掩埋處置方式的偏好增加，以及對特定類型廢棄物禁令，可能會減少本公司掩埋場體積，並導致營業收入與營運結果下降。
總體經濟狀況與消費者趨勢可直接且不利地影響本公司服務的營收、營運毛利及整體財務結果。
醫療廢棄物、管制藥物廢棄物及個人與機密資訊的體積減少，以及醫療產業條件的變化，可能會對本公司財務結果產生不利影響。
適用稅法與規範的變更，或對其解釋，或課徵新稅或提高稅率，可能會增加本公司稅務負擔，並對營運結果與現金流產生不利影響。
柴油燃料供應短缺或柴油燃料價格上漲，將提高本公司營運費用。
科技、智慧財產權與資訊安全風險
若本公司無法開發新服務方案並保護智慧財產權，或競爭對手開發或取得突破性科技的專屬權利，本公司財務結果可能會受影響。
我們越來越依賴科技，若我們的科技失敗，將對我們的業務造成不利影響。
無法適應並管理人工智慧的效益與風險，可能使我們面臨責任或處於劣勢。
重大網路安全事件可能對我們的業務以及與客戶、供應商及員工的關係造成負面影響，並使我們面臨更高的責任風險。
日益嚴格的隱私規範與資料保護相關法規的關注
paragraphs: 本公司之業務、財務狀況及營運成果，受許多風險與不確定因素影響，其中一些目前尚未知悉或未被認為具有重大影響。您應仔細考量下列風險因素，並配合第 7 項「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析」及第 8 項「財務報表與補充資料」之內容。
本公司未來之財務表現與成功，很大程度取決於本公司能否成功執行業務策略。執行此策略將需要有效管理本公司之營運、財務與人力資源，並對這些資源產生重大需求。請參閱第 1 項「業務」以取得更多有關本公司業務策略之資訊。追求此策略可能涉及風險，包括以下各項：
● 本公司員工、客戶或投資人可能不支持或贊成本公司之策略。
● 本公司策略之關鍵要素為透過價格領導地位來實現獲利管理，此一策略在維持現有業務與以合理回報爭取新業務方面已產生挑戰。本公司不願追求低毛利但高成交量之業務，可能對本公司現金流或營運成果產生負面影響。
● 本公司可能無法成功執行以科技為導向之自動化與最佳化策略，以及其他提升營運效率之改進措施，且這些努力可能無法達到預期之結果。
● 本公司可能無法維持透過自動化與最佳化或收購整合所實現之成本節省，原因可能是通貨膨脹所導致之成本壓力或其他因素。
